senses.def: a small useful tool or machine
ex: He loves buying new kitchen gadgets.
This phone is full of clever gadgets.

senses.def: an increase in amount, size or level
ex: There was a gain in weight.
The company announced a big gain in profits.

senses.def: an advantage or profit
ex: He did it for personal gain.

senses.def: to get something useful or valuable, or more of something
ex: She gained a lot of experience.
He gained five kilos in a month.

senses.def: a very strong wind
ex: The gale blew down several trees.
Ships stayed in port because of the gale.

senses.def: a clever action or remark at the start, to get an advantage
ex: His offer was a clever opening gambit.
The company's price cut was a risky gambit.

senses.def: the activity of risking money on the result of a game or race
ex: Gambling is illegal in some countries.
He lost his savings through gambling.

senses.def: an activity with rules that people play for fun
ex: Let's play a game.
Chess is a difficult game.

senses.def: a match between teams or players
ex: We watched the football game.
The game ended in a draw.

senses.def: a group of criminals or young people who cause trouble

He was beaten up by a street gang.

senses.def: a group of friends (informal)
ex: I'm going out with the gang tonight.

senses.def: a member of a violent criminal group
ex: The film is about a famous gangster.
Gangsters controlled the city.

senses.def: an empty space between two things
ex: There is a gap in the fence.

senses.def: a big difference between two groups or ideas
ex: There is a gap between rich and poor.

senses.def: a building where you keep a car

senses.def: a place where cars are repaired or petrol is sold
ex: I took the car to the garage.

senses.def: a person who looks after a garden, as a job or hobby
ex: The gardener cut the grass.

senses.def: a substance like air that burns, used for cooking and heating
ex: We cook with gas.

senses.def: a substance like air that is not solid or liquid
ex: Oxygen is a gas.

senses.def: petrol (US)

senses.def: a quick breath taken in because of surprise or pain

senses.def: a door in a wall or fence outside a building

senses.def: the place in an airport where you get on a plane
ex: Go to gate 12.

senses.def: a way in; an entrance

senses.def: something that gives access to something else

senses.def: to come together in a group, or to bring people together
ex: Everyone gathered in the hall.
Please gather your things.

senses.def: to collect things from different places
ex: She gathered wood for the fire.

senses.def: to understand something from what you have seen or heard
ex: I gather you were away last week.

senses.def: awkward and not knowing how to behave in social situations
ex: He felt gauche at the formal party.

senses.def: sexually attracted to people of the same sex, especially describing men
ex: He is an openly gay actor.
The city has a large gay community.

senses.def: a long, steady look
ex: She felt his gaze on her.
He turned his gaze to the window.

senses.def: the clothes and tools you need for an activity
ex: Don't forget your camping gear.
The player put on his football gear.

senses.def: a part of a vehicle that changes the speed at which it moves
ex: She changed gear to go up the hill.

senses.def: used to express surprise or admiration (informal, US)
ex: Gee, that's a big dog!
Gee, thanks a lot!

senses.def: a valuable stone that has been cut and polished
ex: The crown was covered with gems.

senses.def: a person or thing that is especially good
ex: This little café is a hidden gem.

senses.def: a part of a cell that controls a feature passed from parents to children
ex: Eye colour is controlled by genes.
A faulty gene can cause the illness.

senses.def: not specific or detailed; involving most people or things
ex: He has a good general knowledge.
The general idea is clear.

senses.def: a senior officer in the army
ex: The general gave the order.
He became a general in 1990.

mistake.note: in general is a fixed phrase; generally is an adverb and needs no 'in'.

senses.def: usually; in most cases
ex: I generally wake up at seven.
Generally, the weather here is warm.

senses.def: by most people
ex: It is generally believed to be safe.

senses.def: to produce or create something such as energy or ideas
ex: Wind farms generate electricity.
The film generated a lot of interest.

senses.def: all the people of about the same age
ex: The older generation remembers the war.

senses.def: a stage in the development of a product
ex: This is the latest generation of phones.

senses.def: the quality of being kind and willing to give

senses.def: willing to give money, time or help freely
ex: He is generous with his time.
She made a generous gift to the school.

senses.def: larger than usual
ex: The restaurant serves generous portions.

senses.def: relating to genes or inherited features
ex: The illness has a genetic cause.
Scientists study genetic differences.

senses.def: a person with extremely high intelligence or skill
ex: Einstein was a genius.
She is a musical genius.

senses.def: extremely great natural ability
ex: It was a stroke of genius.

senses.def: the complete set of genes in a living thing
ex: Scientists mapped the human genome.
The genome contains all the instructions for life.

senses.def: a type of art, music, film or writing with a particular style
ex: Science fiction is my favourite genre.

senses.def: a man who is polite and behaves well
ex: He is a real gentleman.
Ladies and gentlemen, welcome!

senses.def: in a soft, careful way
ex: She gently touched his arm.
Handle the glass gently.

senses.def: real and not false or copied

It was a genuine mistake.

senses.def: honest and sincere
ex: She is a genuine person.

senses.def: really; in a sincere way
ex: I am genuinely sorry.
She was genuinely surprised.

senses.def: relating to the study of the Earth's rocks and structure
ex: The area has interesting geological features.
A geological survey found oil.

senses.def: a movement of the hand or head to express a meaning
ex: He made a rude gesture.
She waved her hand in a friendly gesture.

senses.def: something you do to show a feeling
ex: The gift was a kind gesture.

senses.def: to receive or obtain something
ex: I got a letter from my uncle.
Where did you get that bag?

senses.def: to become
ex: It's getting dark.
She got angry.

senses.def: to arrive at a place
ex: We got home at six.

senses.def: a short holiday, especially to escape from normal life
ex: We planned a weekend getaway.
The cabin is a perfect getaway.

senses.def: an escape after a crime
ex: The thieves made their getaway in a van.

senses.def: a part of a city where one group lives, usually in poor conditions
ex: Many families lived in the ghetto.
The city's ghettos suffer from poverty.

senses.def: looking or sounding like a ghost; pale and strange
ex: A ghostly figure stood in the hall.
The fog gave the street a ghostly look.

senses.def: extremely large
ex: They built a giant sandcastle.
A giant wave hit the boat.

senses.def: having a natural ability or great intelligence
ex: She is a gifted pianist.
The school has classes for gifted children.

senses.def: a live music performance
ex: We went to a gig last night.
The band plays gigs every weekend.

senses.def: a short-term job
ex: He found a gig as a driver.

senses.def: a hot-tasting root used as a spice in cooking
ex: Add some ginger to the soup.
She drank ginger tea for her cold.

senses.def: a female child or young woman
ex: The girl is reading a book.
They have two girls.

senses.def: to put something into someone's hand or let them have it
ex: Give me the book.
She gave him a present.

senses.def: to cause or produce something
ex: The sun gives us light.
Exercise gives you energy.

senses.def: to do an action
ex: He gave a speech.
She gave me a hug.

mistake.note: With give, put the person before the thing, with no to: give someone something.

senses.def: to stop trying to do something before you have finished
ex: Don't give up! You're nearly there.
I gave up trying to explain.

senses.def: to stop doing something you do regularly
ex: He gave up smoking last year.
I'm giving up sugar for a month.

mistake.note: give up is followed by -ing, not to-infinitive.

senses.def: already stated or fixed
ex: Write the answer in the given time.
At any given moment, thousands of planes are flying.

senses.def: happy and pleased about something
ex: I'm glad you came.
She was glad to see him.

senses.def: attractive in an exciting, fashionable way
ex: She looked glamorous in her red dress.
He lives a glamorous life.

senses.def: a quick look
ex: She took a quick glance at her watch.
At first glance, the room looked tidy.

senses.def: to look at something for a very short time
ex: He glanced at the clock.
She glanced up from her book.

senses.def: a feeling of happy excitement, often because of good luck
ex: The children shouted with glee.
She clapped her hands in glee.

senses.def: a very quick look at someone or something
ex: I caught a glimpse of the singer.
The book gives a glimpse of life in the past.

senses.def: an attractive, expensive and exciting appearance
ex: The awards night was full of glitz.
She loved the glitz of Hollywood.

senses.def: relating to the whole world
ex: Climate change is a global problem.
It is a global company.

senses.def: dark and not cheerful
ex: It was a gloomy, grey day.
The room looked gloomy.

senses.def: feeling or showing sadness and little hope
ex: He felt gloomy about the future.

senses.def: very beautiful or very enjoyable
ex: We had glorious weather all week.
The view was glorious.

senses.def: deserving great praise and honour
ex: It was a glorious victory.

senses.def: great fame and praise for an achievement
ex: The team won glory for their country.
He dreamed of fame and glory.

senses.def: a soft, steady light
ex: We saw the glow of a fire.
The lamp gave a warm glow.

senses.def: sad and quiet
ex: He looked glum after the loss.
Why are you so glum?

senses.def: to move or travel from one place to another
ex: I go to school by bus.
Let's go home.

senses.def: to leave to do an activity

senses.def: to become, usually something bad
ex: The milk went sour.
He went pale.

senses.def: a turn to do something in a game
ex: It's your go.
Can I have a go?

senses.def: an animal with horns and a beard, kept for milk or meat
ex: The farmer keeps goats on the hill.
Goat cheese is delicious.

senses.def: a being believed to have power over nature and people's lives

Many people believe in God.

mistake.note: believe takes in before God, not to.

senses.def: a female being believed to have special powers
ex: Athena was the Greek goddess of wisdom.
Ancient people prayed to the goddess.

senses.def: having a bright yellow colour like gold
ex: She has long golden hair.
The sand was golden in the sun.

senses.def: made of gold
ex: He wore a golden ring.

senses.def: a game in which players hit a small ball into holes with a club
ex: My uncle plays golf every Sunday.
We watched golf on TV.

senses.def: of a high standard; pleasant
ex: This is a good book.
The food was really good.

senses.def: able to do something well
ex: She is good at maths.

senses.def: kind and well-behaved
ex: He is a good boy.

senses.def: something that is right or helps people
ex: Exercise is good for you.
It's for your own good.

mistake.note: Use good at for a skill.

senses.def: used to show surprise, worry or annoyance
ex: Goodness, is that the time?

senses.def: things that are made to be sold
ex: The shop sells electrical goods.
Goods are delivered by train.

senses.def: a friendly feeling and willingness to help

Her goodwill helped solve the dispute.

senses.def: a large water bird with a long neck, like a duck
ex: Geese flew over the lake.
We had roast goose for dinner.

mistake.note: The plural of goose is geese.

senses.def: a narrow valley with steep rocky sides
ex: A river runs through the gorge.
We walked along the gorge.

senses.def: very beautiful or pleasant
ex: You look gorgeous in that dress.
The weather is gorgeous today.

senses.def: a very large strong ape with black hair
ex: The gorilla ate leaves.
We saw a gorilla at the zoo.

senses.def: talk about other people's private lives, which may not be true
ex: She loves celebrity gossip.
Office gossip spread fast.

senses.def: to talk about other people's private lives

senses.def: relating to high-quality food and drink

They opened a gourmet restaurant.

senses.def: a person who knows a lot about good food and drink

senses.def: a painful disease that makes the joints, especially the toes, swell

senses.def: a person who is in charge of a state, region or institution
ex: The governor opened the new hospital.

senses.def: a long, formal dress for a woman
ex: She wore a beautiful evening gown.

senses.def: a loose piece of clothing worn for a special purpose
ex: The students wore graduation gowns.

senses.def: to take hold of something suddenly and roughly
ex: He grabbed my arm.
She grabbed her bag and ran.

senses.def: to get something quickly because you are in a hurry
ex: Let's grab a coffee.

senses.def: a smooth and beautiful way of moving
ex: The dancer moved with grace.
She walked with natural grace.

senses.def: polite and kind behaviour

senses.def: the time when you receive a degree after finishing your studies
ex: Her parents came to her graduation.

senses.def: to join a piece of a plant or body tissue to another

ex: She needed a skin graft.

senses.def: the seeds of crops such as wheat, rice and corn
ex: The farmers harvest grain in autumn.
The country grows wheat and other grain.

senses.def: a very small piece of something hard

senses.def: large and impressive
ex: They stayed in a grand hotel.
The palace has a grand entrance.

senses.def: most important
ex: He won the grand prize.

senses.def: an amount of money given by the government or an organisation for a purpose
ex: She received a grant to study abroad.
The school got a government grant.

senses.def: to formally give or allow something
ex: The court granted him permission.

senses.def: a large round yellow fruit with a sour taste
ex: I have grapefruit for breakfast.
She drank a glass of grapefruit juice.

senses.def: an understanding of a subject or situation
ex: He has a good grasp of grammar.
The idea is beyond my grasp.

senses.def: a firm hold on something
ex: She held the rope in a tight grasp.

senses.def: feeling or showing thanks for something done for you
ex: I am grateful for your help.

mistake.right: I am grateful for your help.
mistake.note: grateful for a thing, grateful to a person.

senses.def: the feeling of being thankful
ex: She showed her gratitude with a gift.
I want to express my gratitude.

senses.def: a place in the ground where a dead person is buried

senses.def: very good; wonderful

senses.def: large in size, amount or degree

senses.def: to feel great sadness, especially after a death
ex: The family is still grieving.

senses.def: a flat metal frame for cooking food over heat

senses.def: serious and unhappy
ex: He had a grim look on his face.

senses.def: unpleasant and depressing

senses.def: a wide smile

senses.def: a firm hold of something

ex: He gripped the steering wheel.

ex: The story gripped me.

senses.def: a man who is getting married

senses.def: a person who shows tourists around a place

senses.def: a man (informal)

senses.def: a member of a travelling people (the word is often considered offensive; Roma is preferred)
